Cindy Quicaña Silvia Conde

Passionate about creativity, with a profound focus on science through engineering, technological innovation, and a commitment to artistic expression.

I value my experiences, learnings, and discoveries, which I enjoyed from two perspectives:

  • Participating in programs such as The Knowledge Society (TKS) '25 or Future Generation of Scientists (FGS) '24; serving as Outreach Officer at the Center for Strategic Innovation and Future (CSIF); working on innovation projects, either within a team sharing a common vision, such as 3DR at SIFT 2023–24, or individually, developing a project based on BCI (soon to be presented in a moonshot); taking part and becoming a semifinalist in the Russian Mathematics Olympiad SAMMAT or in the Global Spring Challenge organized by Microsoft, Samsung, and Maverick Biometals; and assuming the role of presenter at a UN ECOSOC Youth Global Forum side event, addressing the current impact of NGOs and NPOs across countries in solving the SDGs of the 2030 Agenda through innovation.
  • From more personal and modest projects, such as cultivating microalgae, practicing taxidermy, building Python executables to control my PC through eye-tracking, 3D printing and modeling with Blender 4.2, to volunteering in local beach cleanups.

In parallel, the arts have been another factor that has given space to my convictions, particularly the visual arts: drawing and painting, which I have enjoyed since the age of four.

We have all made strokes as children, even before speaking properly. My earliest artistic expressions, as with many others, were those first strokes, and I find them very important because I consider them a fundamental form of human expression, one that has transcended civilizations and surpasses the barriers of written language. More than an attempt to replicate something from real life on paper, it is a dynamic way of communicating my ideas, emotions, and experiences, and through color, the message can be expanded. I value that it allows us to explore creatively our understanding of the world.

Thus, my performance here has been more personal than about involvement in school contests in mid school, the Peruvian Juegos Florales contest during the pandemic and in 2024, or the sale of commissioned works.
